summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style entry on Wiraqucha, a mountain in the Andes of Peru, located in the Cusco Region's Quispicanchi Province. It lists the mountain's position relative to nearby districts and peaks, and notes the Willkanuta River and the Quyllur Urmana lake. The note also gives the word's Quechua meanings, including a god, a sir or gentleman, and an Inca emperor.
one_line: Wiraqucha is a Peruvian Andean mountain in Cusco's Quispicanchi Province, near the Willkanuta River and Quyllur Urmana lake.
key_facts: Wiraqucha is a mountain in the Andes of Peru.
Wiraqucha is situated in the Cusco Region, Quispicanchi Province.
Wiraqucha lies in the districts Andahuaylillas, Huaro and Urcos.
Wiraqucha is south-east of the higher mountain named Quri.
The Willkanuta River flows along the mountain Wiraqucha.
The lake Quyllur Urmana lies at the feet of Wiraqucha.
In Quechua, "wira" means fat and "qucha" means lake.
Wiraqucha can mean mister, sir or gentleman in Quechua.
Wiraqucha was one of the greatest Andean divinities.
Wiraqucha was also the eighth emperor of the Tawantinsuyu (Wiraqucha Inka).
The name is also spelled "Wiracocha" and Hispanicized as "Huirajochan".
